name: Grilled village chicken
summary: A small free-range bird grilled whole over charcoal and eaten with cơm lam. Go Vietnam ties it to Kon Tum by the Đăk Bla and to Măng Đen. The printed prices do not match.
origin: Go Vietnam calls grilled chicken with cơm lam the pairing of former Kon Tum, raised by Ba Na and Xơ Đăng families.
taste: Go Vietnam’s grilled-chicken article describes golden skin, charcoal smoke, firm sweet meat, lemongrass, and wild chili, then a sharp heat from green-chili salt or muối é.
howToEat: Tear the chicken by hand, dip it, and eat it with a piece of cơm lam, often with forest greens and cucumber. Eat it hot, off the charcoal. The grilled-chicken article says the bird is about 1–1.5 kg, clamped in bamboo splints, and marinated with lemongrass, wild chili, salt, garlic, and shallots, sometimes brushed with forest honey. The dip is green-chili salt, wild-pepper salt, or muối é.

The cluster article is a different marinade and a different price. Kon K’Tu chicken is marinated with jar wine, garlic, lemongrass, lime leaves, and chili salt, and grilled 30–40 minutes. That article prints 280,000–400,000 VND for a 1.2 kg bird, enough for 4 people.

The grilled-chicken article prints about 220,000–280,000 VND a bird, and 150,000–250,000 VND for a set with cơm lam, as a 2025 reference. Go Vietnam’s Măng Đen article prints a Sedang set with forest é leaf and fresh forest honey at 350,000–600,000 VND for 4 people. The figures stay. Check on arrival.
where: Kon Tum beside the Đăk Bla, Kon K’Tu, and Măng Đen in Kon Plông. The grilled-chicken article also names the dry months, roughly November to April, as the season that suits Măng Đen. The dish is served year-round on that article, and at festivals and new-house meals in the villages.
seoTitle: Grilled chicken in Kon Tum — with bamboo rice
seoDescription: Free-range chicken grilled over charcoal with cơm lam. Go Vietnam prints 280,000–400,000, 220,000–280,000, and a Măng Đen set of 350,000–600,000 VND.
